tool_input.commit_message:
Closes ethos-bfml, ethos-hy40, ethos-kcbv, ethos-e05k, ethos-jw1z.

Cluster 3's unifying defect: a check that reports success without having
verified the thing it claims to check. Five beads, plus 17 review
findings from Copilot, qodo, and Cursor Bugbot.

- kcbv: hasActiveSealCall's lexical shell scanner replaced with
  execution-based verification (DES-077), honouring the stop-loss
  declared after four patch rounds.
- bfml/hy40: one defect, not two. Presence is now checked for both the
  seal and trailer hooks on an enabled repo. CheckHookCurrency's
  PASS-on-absence is deliberately unchanged — correct for a currency
  check on a dormant repo.
- e05k: new check flags deployed archetypes missing
  require_delegated_worker, deriving the monitored set from the embedded
  seed content rather than a hand-maintained list.
- jw1z: orphaned-agent FAIL distinguishes a stale generated file from a
  genuine orphan.

Review findings of note: the archetype guard silently dropped the global
layer and PASSed on an install it never inspected when os.UserHomeDir()
failed; the sandbox executed hooks lacking the exec bit that git would
never run; and its invocation log was both forgeable and argv-lossy, so
a hook that never called ethos could fabricate a match.

Three Windows defects reached review with every check green, one of them
introduced by this branch. DES-077 records the common cause as a
standing fact: no runner is Windows, so no Windows runtime behaviour is
observable in CI. Every Windows guard here is verified by construction —
a build tag, a seam override, or a citation of Go's own source — never
by observation. Tracked as ethos-ell5.

The final finding was the most valuable. Tying the sandbox's platform
guard to its build tag (sandboxSupported, declared in the same tagged
file pair as the process-group primitives) revealed that one variable
had been standing in for two different facts: whether FileMode carries
execute bits (Windows only) and whether the sandbox can run at all
(non-unix). On plan9 those disagree. Three green tests went red on the
switch, proving the conflation rather than arguing it.

Behavioural note: a non-unix, non-Windows platform now refuses to
execute where it previously would have tried. Blast radius is zero — no
such platform builds this package.

Residual left open and documented rather than partially patched: a
setsid-detached hook child escapes process-group cleanup. No portable,
unprivileged containment exists across shipped targets, and lifetime
containment was never the security boundary — hook execution is
untrusted-code execution by design.

Also swept under fix-the-class: two misattached godoc comments (one in
cmd/ethos/session.go, outside this branch's diff) and four Unix-only
test assumptions, two of which predate the branch.

  Cluster 3's unifying defect was a check that reports success without
  having verified the thing it claims to check. That shape recurred
  inside the fix itself more than once — an archetype guard that
  swallowed load errors into a green PASS, a hardcoded list that could
  only monitor what someone remembered to add, and a fallback treating
  "I could not determine X" as "X is the default."

  plan9/js compile break that predates the branch at internal/process,
  and one duplicate filed against a commit that had already been fixed.

  classifications were wrong — the documented rationale answered a
  different question than the finding asked.

  (Windows only) and whether the sandbox can run at all (non-unix). On

  switch, proving the conflation rather than arguing it.
